title: Does p-Hacking Mitigate or Exacerbate the Effects of Publication Bias?
abstract: arXiv:2609.05372v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies the effects of p-hacking on the bias of published estimates when papers with statistically significant results are selectively published. We show that fast p-hacking---actions that lead to large changes in p-values---always exacerbates the bias from selective publication. On the other hand, slow p-hacking---actions that lead to small changes in p-values---exacerbates bias when selection is weak, but mitigates it when selection is strong. In a model featuring both types of p-hacking, we show that a normality assumption identifies the true distribution of effects as well as the counterfactual mean that would obtain under selective publication without p-hacking. Applying the model to meta-analyses on the effects of behavioral nudges and development aid, we find suggestive evidence that both mitigation and exacerbation can arise in practice.

translated_title: p值操纵是缓解还是加剧了发表偏倚的影响？
translated_abstract: 本文研究了当具有统计显著性结果的论文被选择性发表时，p值操纵对已发表估计值偏差的影响。我们表明，快速p值操纵——即导致p值发生大幅变化的操作——总是会加剧选择性发表造成的偏差。另一方面，缓慢p值操纵——即导致p值发生微小变化的操作——在选择压力较弱时会加剧偏差，但在选择压力较强时会缓解偏差。在一个同时包含两种p值操纵的模型中，我们证明了正态性假设能够识别效应的真实分布，以及在不存在p值操纵的选择性发表情形下的反事实均值。将该模型应用于关于行为助推和发展援助效应的元分析中，我们发现了提示性证据，表明缓解与加剧效应在实践中都可能存在。
tldr: 本文区分了快速与缓慢两种p值操纵方式，发现快速p值操纵总是加剧选择性发表造成的偏差，而缓慢p值操纵在发表选择压力较强时反而能缓解偏差，并基于正态性假设提出了识别真实效应分布的模型方法。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that fast p-hacking always exacerbates bias from selective publication, while slow p-hacking mitigates it under strong selection, and proposes a normality-based model to identify the true distribution of effects.
